instruments.title: Information Technology (Intermediary Guidelines and Digital Media Ethics Code) Rules, 2021, Part II

notifications.note: Principal rules. Read from a copy of the gazette PDF hosted by PRS, not from egazette.gov.in.
Sets fifty lakh registered users in India as the significant social media intermediary threshold under rule 2(1)(v).
Substituted rule 3(1)(a), (b), (f) and 3(2)(a)(i); inserted 3(1)(m), (n) and rule 3A.
Online gaming and fact-check amendments; renumbered 3(1)(b) to sub-clauses (i)-(xi); added the 'prominently publish' Explanation to rule 3(2).

In force 15 November 2025. Substituted rule 3(1)(d): actual knowledge arises only by a court order or a reasoned written intimation from an authorised senior officer, and intimations are reviewed every month by a Secretary-level officer.
In force 20 February 2026. Synthetically generated information, and the shorter clocks in rule 3(1)(c), 3(1)(d), 3(2)(a)(i) and 3(2)(b).

Corrigendum to G.S.R. 120(E). In rule 3(1)(c)(iii) and rule 3(1)(ca)(ii)(IV), for 'the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023', read 'the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 read with the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023'. Seen only as a footnote in the consolidated text hosted by MIB, not in the gazette.

instruments.title: Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) Rules, 2020, grievance duties only

notifications.note: NOT READ. A legal database footnote says it substituted rule 4(1) (nodal officer) only. Rule 4(1) is left out of this catalog for that reason.

rules.obligation: Prominently publish the rules and regulations, privacy policy and user agreement on the website, the app or both, in English or an Eighth Schedule language of the user's choice, and ensure compliance with them.
evidence_hints: Footer and legal page templates
Routes for terms, privacy and community guidelines
Links on the signup screen and the app's settings

rules.obligation: Inform users of those documents and make reasonable efforts, by itself and through its users, that nobody hosts or shares information that: (i) belongs to another person and to which the user has no right; (ii) is obscene, pornographic, paedophilic, invasive of another's privacy including bodily privacy, insulting or harassing on the basis of gender, racially or ethnically objectionable, relates to or encourages money laundering or gambling, is an online game that causes user harm, or promotes enmity between groups on grounds of religion or caste with intent to incite violence; (iii) is harmful to a child; (iv) infringes a patent, trademark, copyright or other proprietary right; (v) deceives or misleads the addressee about the origin of a message, or knowingly and intentionally communicates misinformation or information that is patently false and untrue or misleading; (vi) impersonates another person; (vii) threatens the unity, integrity, defence, security or sovereignty of India, friendly relations with foreign States or public order, causes incitement to a cognisable offence, prevents investigation of an offence, or insults another nation; (viii) contains a virus or other code designed to interrupt, destroy or limit a computer resource; (ix), (x) concerns online games that are not permissible; (xi) violates any law.
evidence_hints: The prohibited content clause in the terms or community guidelines
Report and moderation flows that act on those categories
rules.note: Sub-clauses (ix) and (x), and the online game limb of (ii), came from G.S.R. 275(E). Whether later online gaming legislation changed them was not checked. Sub-clause (v) also prints a limb on information that a notified Central Government fact check unit identifies as fake, false or misleading. The Bombay High Court struck that limb down in Kunal Kamra v. Union of India (September 2024); the Union's appeal is before the Supreme Court, which refused a stay. That status comes from court reporting, not from the orders. The obligation above leaves the limb out for that reason.

rules.obligation: Periodically tell users, in a simple and effective manner, that: (i) on non-compliance with the terms the intermediary may terminate or suspend access immediately, or remove the information, or both; (ii) a user responsible for unlawful information may face penalty or punishment under the IT Act or other law; (iii) offences that must be reported under a law such as the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 read with the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, or the POCSO Act, will be reported to the appropriate authority.
rules.deadline: At least once every three months
evidence_hints: A scheduled job, cron entry or campaign that sends the reminder, and its interval
The reminder template: does it carry all three limbs
A log showing the last sends
rules.note: Was once every year before 20 February 2026. Limb (iii) is stated as corrected by the corrigendum G.S.R. 148(E) of 26 February 2026, which was read in a consolidated text and not in the gazette.

rules.obligation: Where the product lets users create or share synthetically generated information, additionally tell users that: (i) using it to make unlawful synthetic content under rule 3(3)(a)(i) may attract penalty or punishment under the laws the clause lists; (ii) a contravention may lead to removal of the content, suspension or termination of the account, disclosure of the user's identity to a victim complainant in accordance with law, and mandatory reporting.
rules.deadline: No separate period stated; read with the three-monthly notice in Rule 3(1)(c)
evidence_hints: Terms, AI feature policy and the generator's own screens
The rule 3(1)(c) reminder template

rules.obligation: On becoming aware, on its own, through actual knowledge or through a grievance, of a violation of rule 3(3) involving synthetically generated information, take expeditious and appropriate action, including removal, account suspension, identity disclosure to a victim in accordance with law, and mandatory reporting.
evidence_hints: A report category for AI-generated or deepfake content
The moderation playbook for synthetic media
Account action code paths

rules.obligation: On actual knowledge that information on its computer resource is used to commit an unlawful act prohibited by law (in relation to the sovereignty and integrity of India, the security of the State, friendly relations with foreign States, public order, decency or morality, contempt of court, defamation, incitement to these, or any other information prohibited by law), remove or disable access to it. Actual knowledge arises only: (i) by an order of a court of competent jurisdiction; or (ii) by a reasoned intimation in writing that (I) is issued by an officer whom the Appropriate Government or its agency has authorised by order in writing, not below the rank of Joint Secretary or equivalent, or a Director or equivalent where no such rank is appointed, and, for the police, by an officer not below Deputy Inspector General who is specially authorised; and (II) clearly specifies the legal basis and statutory provision invoked, the nature of the unlawful act, and the specific URL, identifier or other electronic location to be removed. An officer not below Secretary reviews such intimations once every month.
rules.deadline: Within 3 hours of receiving the actual knowledge: the court order or the intimation
evidence_hints: An admin action that disables content by URL or ID
A runbook for court orders and government intimations
A runbook step that reads an intimation against the rule's conditions: written, reasoned, the issuing officer's rank and written authorisation, the legal basis, the specific URL
An on-call route that is staffed outside office hours
An audit log of who disabled what and when
SLA constants still set to 36 hours
rules.note: Was 36 hours before 20 February 2026. G.S.R. 775(E) substituted the clause from 15 November 2025; G.S.R. 120(E) then changed the clock, added 'by order in writing' and allowed more than one authorised police officer. The rule does not say what an intermediary should do with an intimation that falls short of these conditions, and the three hours leave little time to ask: that is a question for counsel.

rules.obligation: Periodically inform users, in English or an Eighth Schedule language of their choice, of the rules and regulations, privacy policy or user agreement, or of any change to them.
evidence_hints: A change-notice email or in-app banner
A changelog or version date on the legal pages
rules.note: G.S.R. 120(E) did not amend this clause. The three-monthly duty is Rule 3(1)(c).

rules.obligation: Where information is removed or disabled under rule 3(1)(d), voluntarily under 3(1)(b), or on a grievance, preserve it and the associated records for investigation, without vitiating the evidence.
rules.deadline: 180 days, or longer if a court or an authorised agency requires
evidence_hints: Delete or purge jobs that touch removed, hidden or moderated content
Retention settings on object storage and moderation tables
Whether 'associated records' such as uploader, timestamps and logs survive
rules.note: Overlaps with the DPDP Act. Sections 8(7) and 12(3) of that Act except retention necessary for compliance with a law in force, and this clause is such a law for its 180 days. Those sections come into force in May 2027 under G.S.R. 843(E) of 13 November 2025. What may be kept after day 180, and which records the clause reaches, are questions for counsel. nodal reports the overlap and refers to Vigil; it does not resolve it.

rules.obligation: Retain the information collected from a user for registration after the registration is cancelled or withdrawn.
evidence_hints: Account closure and deletion jobs
What happens to the registration fields: email, phone, signup metadata
rules.note: Overlaps with the DPDP Act. Sections 8(7) and 12(3) of that Act except retention necessary for compliance with a law in force, and this clause is such a law for its 180 days. Those sections come into force in May 2027 under G.S.R. 843(E) of 13 November 2025. What may be kept after day 180, and which records the clause reaches, are questions for counsel. nodal reports the overlap and refers to Vigil; it does not resolve it.

rules.obligation: Provide information under its control, or assistance, to a lawfully authorised Government agency for identity verification, or for the prevention, detection, investigation or prosecution of offences, or for cyber security incidents. The order must be in writing and state its purpose.
rules.deadline: As soon as possible, and within 72 hours of receiving the order
evidence_hints: A law enforcement request runbook
An intake address or portal for agencies
A register of requests and response times
rules.note: G.S.R. 275(E) set 24 hours for online gaming intermediaries offering permissible real money games. Online gaming is not checked.

rules.obligation: Prominently publish the name of the Grievance Officer, their contact details and the mechanism by which a user or victim can complain. 'Prominently publish' means clearly visible on the home page or home screen, or on a page directly accessible from it.
evidence_hints: Footer, contact, help and legal templates
The live site's home page and the pages one click from it
A generic support email with no named officer
A complaint form or address

rules.obligation: The Grievance Officer acknowledges each complaint.
evidence_hints: An automatic acknowledgement on intake
A ticket reference in the acknowledgement
Acknowledgement SLA values in config

rules.obligation: The Grievance Officer resolves each complaint.
evidence_hints: Resolution SLA constants and due-date arithmetic
Values still set to 15 days
Escalation jobs keyed to the due date

rules.obligation: A complaint that asks for removal of information or a link relating to rule 3(1)(b), other than sub-clauses (i), (iv) and (xi), is acted on as expeditiously as possible. The intermediary may build safeguards against misuse.
rules.deadline: Resolved within 36 hours of the report
evidence_hints: A separate SLA for removal or content complaints
Values still set to 72 hours
How a complaint is routed to the faster queue
rules.note: Was 72 hours before 20 February 2026. The excluded sub-clauses are another person's information, intellectual property and the residual 'violates any law'.

rules.obligation: The Grievance Officer receives and acknowledges any order, notice or direction from the Appropriate Government, a competent authority or a court.
evidence_hints: A monitored address or portal for orders
Who is named as the recipient in the runbook

rules.obligation: On a complaint by an individual, or anyone on their behalf, about content that prima facie exposes their private area, shows them in full or partial nudity or in a sexual act, or impersonates them in electronic form, including artificially morphed images, take all reasonable and practicable measures to remove or disable access to it.
evidence_hints: A dedicated report category and queue
The SLA constant for that queue: values still set to 24 hours
Out-of-hours staffing or automation for that queue

rules.obligation: Implement a mechanism to receive complaints under rule 3(2)(b) that lets the individual give the details needed about the content or link.
evidence_hints: The report form's categories and fields
Whether a non-user or a representative can file

rules.obligation: A person aggrieved by the Grievance Officer's decision, or whose grievance was not resolved in time, may appeal to the Grievance Appellate Committee. The rules read do not require the intermediary to tell users about this route, so a closure message that omits it is a good-practice gap, not a breach.
rules.deadline: Appeal within 30 days of receiving the Grievance Officer's communication
evidence_hints: Closure and rejection templates
The grievance page

rules.obligation: Comply with every order of the Grievance Appellate Committee and upload a report of that compliance on the website.
evidence_hints: A runbook step for Committee orders
A page or section where compliance reports are posted

rules.obligation: Deploy reasonable and appropriate technical measures, including automated tools, so that no user can create or share synthetically generated information that violates the law, including content that: (I) is child sexual abuse material, non-consensual intimate imagery, or obscene or sexually explicit; (II) creates a false document or false electronic record; (III) relates to explosives, arms or ammunition; (IV) falsely depicts a real person or event in a way likely to deceive.
evidence_hints: Prompt and output filters on every generation path, including image-to-image, edit and API routes
Classifier thresholds and bypass flags
What happens when the filter service is down

rules.obligation: Every other piece of synthetically generated information carries a prominent label that is easily noticeable in the visual display, or a prominently prefixed audio disclosure for audio, and is embedded with permanent metadata or another provenance mechanism, to the extent technically feasible, including a unique identifier of the intermediary's computer resource used to make it.
evidence_hints: Where the label is drawn or attached
Metadata writing at generation: C2PA, XMP, EXIF or a custom tag
A unique identifier per asset or per generator
Audio outputs: is the disclosure at the start
rules.note: The notified text sets no size or duration for the label.

rules.obligation: Do not enable the modification, suppression or removal of that label, the permanent metadata or the unique identifier.
evidence_hints: Any code path that strips metadata: image pipelines, thumbnailers, CDN transforms, re-encoders
Feature flags or paid tiers that hide the label
Crop, export and download tools

rules.obligation: Appoint a Chief Compliance Officer: key managerial personnel or another senior employee, resident in India, responsible for compliance with the Act and rules. That officer is liable in any proceedings relating to relevant third-party information, data or communication link made available or hosted by the intermediary where the officer fails to ensure that the intermediary observes due diligence. No liability may be imposed without an opportunity of being heard.
rules.deadline: No period for an intermediary that reaches the threshold today. The three months in the rule ran from the notification of the threshold on 25 February 2021 and ended in May 2021
evidence_hints: The contact or legal page naming the officer
Internal role documents
rules.note: The rule requires the appointment. Rule 4(5) and Rule 3(2)(a) are what require details to be published. The rule states no period for an intermediary that crosses fifty lakh registered users after May 2021. Whether any period is implied is a question for counsel; the text gives none.

rules.obligation: Appoint a nodal contact person for 24x7 coordination with law enforcement: an employee other than the Chief Compliance Officer, resident in India.
rules.deadline: No period for an intermediary that reaches the threshold today. The three months in the rule ran from the notification of the threshold on 25 February 2021 and ended in May 2021
evidence_hints: The contact page or law enforcement guidelines naming the role
An on-call rota that is 24x7
rules.note: The rule states no period for an intermediary that crosses fifty lakh registered users after May 2021. Whether any period is implied is a question for counsel; the text gives none.

rules.obligation: Appoint a Resident Grievance Officer: an employee resident in India who performs the Grievance Officer's functions under rule 3(2).
rules.deadline: No period for an intermediary that reaches the threshold today. The three months in the rule ran from the notification of the threshold on 25 February 2021 and ended in May 2021
evidence_hints: The grievance page: is the named officer described as resident in India
rules.note: The rule states no period for an intermediary that crosses fifty lakh registered users after May 2021. Whether any period is implied is a question for counsel; the text gives none.

rules.obligation: Publish a periodic compliance report with the complaints received and the action taken, and the number of links or items removed through proactive monitoring with automated tools.
evidence_hints: A report job and its schedule
A report template and where it is published
Past reports on the site

rules.obligation: Before any information is displayed, uploaded or published: (a) require the user to declare whether it is synthetically generated; (b) deploy appropriate technical measures to verify that declaration; (c) where either confirms it, display it with a clear and prominent label or notice. Knowingly permitting, promoting or failing to act on such content is deemed a failure of due diligence.
evidence_hints: The upload and post forms: is there a declaration field
The post model: is the declaration stored
A detector or provenance check on upload
How a declared or detected item is rendered

rules.obligation: Deploy appropriate technical measures, including automated tools, to proactively identify depictions of rape or child sexual abuse and copies of information already removed under rule 3(1)(d), show a notice to users who try to access it, keep human oversight, and review the tools periodically for accuracy, fairness, bias and privacy impact.
evidence_hints: Hash matching or classifier services on upload
A review record for the automated tools

rules.obligation: Have a physical contact address in India, published on the website, the app or both, for receiving communications.
evidence_hints: Contact, legal and grievance pages
An address outside India, or a registered office that is not offered as a contact address

rules.obligation: Run a complaint mechanism that gives every complaint or grievance a unique ticket number so the complainant can track it, and, to the extent reasonable, give the complainant reasons for any action taken or not taken.
evidence_hints: Ticket number generation on intake
A status page or status endpoint
Closure templates: do they carry reasons

rules.obligation: Where the intermediary removes or disables information under rule 3(1)(b) on its own accord: (a) notify the user beforehand with the action and the reasons; (b) give the user an adequate and reasonable opportunity to dispute it and ask for reinstatement; (c) have the Resident Grievance Officer oversee that dispute mechanism.
rules.deadline: Notice before removal; dispute decided within a reasonable time
evidence_hints: Moderation code paths that remove content without a notification call
An appeal or reinstatement route for the uploader

rules.obligation: Display prominently, in a clear and accessible manner: the legal name of the entity, the address of its headquarters and branches, its website, and contact details such as email, landline and mobile numbers of customer care and of the grievance officer.
evidence_hints: Footer, contact and about pages
The seller or company information block at checkout
rules.note: The sub-clause letters did not survive text extraction from the gazette PDF, so cite Rule 4(2) without a letter.

rules.obligation: Establish a grievance redressal mechanism adequate to the number of grievances ordinarily received from India, appoint a grievance officer for consumer grievances, and display that officer's name, contact details and designation on the platform.
evidence_hints: A grievance page naming the officer with a designation
A generic support address with no named officer
A complaint intake route

rules.obligation: Ensure the grievance officer acknowledges every consumer complaint and redresses it.
rules.deadline: Acknowledge within 48 hours; redress within one month of receipt
evidence_hints: Acknowledgement automation
SLA constants for consumer complaints
Escalation before the one-month mark

rules.obligation: A marketplace gives a ticket number for each complaint lodged, through which the consumer can track its status.
evidence_hints: Ticket number generation
A complaint status page

rules.obligation: A marketplace displays prominently information on return, refund, exchange, warranty, delivery, payment and the grievance redressal mechanism.
evidence_hints: Help and policy pages linked from product and checkout pages

rules.obligation: An inventory entity displays prominently accurate information on return, refund, exchange, warranty, delivery, payment and the grievance redressal mechanism.
evidence_hints: Help and policy pages linked from product and checkout pages

rules.obligation: An inventory entity gives a ticket number for each complaint lodged, through which the consumer can track its status.
evidence_hints: Ticket number generation
A complaint status page
